pageCache.pageTitle: Performing arts in years 7 & 8 | Great Walstead School
pageCache.text:
Performing Arts
In Years 7 and 8, the Performing Arts take on a new depth and purpose. Pupils refine their skills in art, music and drama, developing confidence, creativity and leadership along the way. With inspiring performance opportunities and access to our on-site Art Studio, they are encouraged to explore their passions and express themselves with growing independence.
Drama
In Years 7 and 8, drama becomes a space for pupils to stretch their creativity and explore performance with increasing independence. They take on a variety of projects, from devising original pieces to exploring classic and contemporary scripts.
Collaboration, communication and confidence sit at the heart of every lesson. Pupils are encouraged to direct, perform and critique with empathy and maturity, skills that prepare them for both senior school and life beyond the stage.There are numerous opportunities to perform throughout the year, culminating in the full-scale school production, a highlight of the Performing Arts calendar that brings together pupils from across the upper years. Regular theatre trips, workshops and specialist masterclasses also deepen understanding and inspire ambition.
Music
By Years 7 and 8, music at Great Walstead is both personal and purposeful. Pupils refine their technical and performance skills while deepening their understanding of theory, composition and musical history.
Alongside curriculum lessons, many pupils take individual instrumental and vocal tuition, and contribute to our rich musical life through ensembles, the chamber choir and the school orchestra. These groups perform regularly at concerts and services throughout the year, developing teamwork, leadership and a lifelong appreciation of music.
Our Performing Arts Thursdays continue to showcase pupil talent, with informal performances offering a platform to share music and drama with peers in a supportive, creative environment.
Art
In the final years at Great Walstead, art becomes a powerful way for pupils to express individuality and develop a personal creative style. Working in our dedicated art studio alongside specialist teachers and artists in residence, they experiment with a range of media including painting, printmaking, mixed media and sculpture.
Pupils are encouraged to think critically, explore ideas with depth and prepare portfolios for art scholarships or future creative study. They also take part in collaborative exhibitions and community art projects that develop both artistic confidence and creative thinking.
This hands-on, exploratory approach helps pupils see art not just as a subject, but as a skill for life - one that fosters resilience, imagination and self-expression.

SEN (Supported Learning)
Building Independence and Confidence
As pupils move into Years 7 and 8, our focus shifts towards independence, self-awareness and preparing for the next stage of learning. The Learning Enhancement Department continues to provide tailored support to ensure every pupil can reach their potential with confidence and pride.
Our Learning Enhancement Department sits at the heart of the school, offering a calm, supportive space for pupils to develop both academically and personally. The team of specialist teachers works closely with subject staff to ensure that each pupil’s needs are understood and met within the classroom environment.
In these final years, we encourage pupils to take greater ownership of their learning. With guidance from staff, they develop strategies for organisation, study skills and managing workload; vital preparation for senior school life. Where appropriate, small group or one-to-one sessions offer focused help with core literacy and numeracy, as well as support for any specific learning differences.
We continue to offer investigations, assessments and advice to help identify strengths and areas for development. When specialist input is required, we support families in accessing trusted professionals such as educational psychologists, speech and language therapists or occupational therapists.
Parents remain central to this process. Regular communication, progress updates and information sessions ensure we work in partnership to support every child’s journey.
At Great Walstead, we are proud of the determination and progress shown by our pupils. By combining high expectations with genuine care, we help them move on to senior school as confident, capable and resilient learners.
With the right support and encouragement, every pupil can achieve more than they ever imagined.
ISI Report 2025 Highlights
"Pupils who have special educational needs and/or disabilities receive individual support in lessons and make consistently good progress." Independent Schools Inspectorate, November 2025

pageCache.pageTitle: Academic - Ready for What Comes Next | Great Walstead School
pageCache.text:
Academic
Ready for What Comes Next
Building independence, depth of knowledge and confidence for senior school and beyond.
A Confident Step into Senior School
In Years 7 and 8, academic learning at Great Walstead takes on a new energy and purpose. Pupils are encouraged to think more deeply, question more boldly and take greater ownership of their learning. With small classes and specialist teachers across every subject, they are supported to develop the study habits, curiosity and independence that prepare them for senior school life.
The focus shifts towards critical thinking, problem solving and applying knowledge with confidence. Lessons stretch and challenge pupils, while still maintaining the warmth and encouragement that define the Great Walstead experience.
Stretch, Challenge and Scholarship Preparation
For many, these final two years bring opportunities to prepare for scholarship applications in academics, sport, music or art. Teachers work closely with each pupil to nurture their talents, provide targeted support and build confidence for assessments and interviews. This tailored approach ensures that every child can achieve their potential and take pride in their achievements.
We are proud of our record of success, with pupils gaining scholarships and awards to leading senior schools including Brighton College, Ardingly College, Hurstpierpoint College, Worth School and beyond.
Skills for Life
Beyond subject mastery, our aim is to help pupils develop the qualities that will carry them far beyond the classroom. The 7Cs – curiosity, courage, creativity, collaboration, compassion, commitment and confidence – continue to shape every aspect of learning. By the time they leave Great Walstead, pupils have learned not only how to succeed in exams, but how to think for themselves, persevere through challenges and take joy in discovery.
A Love of Learning That Lasts
Years 7 and 8 are a time to celebrate just how far each pupil has come – and to inspire a lifelong love of learning. Whether they are debating in English, investigating in science or tackling a new language, every lesson encourages curiosity and confidence. Pupils leave Great Walstead ready for their next chapter, grounded in strong values, equipped with deep knowledge and prepared to take on the world with enthusiasm and integrity.
ISI Report 2025 Highlights
“Leaders respond well to the school council and implement changes which improve pupils’ experiences.” Independent Schools Inspectorate, November 2025
“Pupils are provided with suitable opportunities to accept responsibilities and develop leadership skills.” Independent Schools Inspectorate, November 2025

pageCache.pageTitle: Sport In Years 7 and 8 | Great Walstead School
pageCache.text:
Sport
Challenge, competition and confidence
In Years 7 and 8, sport is about challenge, competition and confidence. Pupils build on firm foundations, taking pride in representing their school, developing leadership skills and preparing for future sporting success at senior school and beyond.
In Years 7 and 8, sport takes on a new level of challenge and ambition. Pupils refine their technical skills, take on leadership roles and compete with growing confidence in both team and individual disciplines.
Our specialist sports staff prepare pupils for the next stage of their sporting journey, helping them to aim high in inter-school competitions and, where appropriate, to work towards sports scholarships at senior schools. Training sessions focus on performance, resilience and tactical understanding, while maintaining the balance of fun and friendship that defines sport at Great Walstead.
Swimming continues in our on-site pool, where pupils build stamina and skill through both lessons and competitive galas. Games afternoons and fixtures allow every child to take part, whether competing at a high level or simply enjoying the thrill of being part of a team.
By this stage, pupils are developing independence, leadership and the ability to motivate others. They leave Great Walstead with not only strong sporting foundations but also the confidence, discipline and team spirit that will serve them for life.
Our approach to teaching sport
Listen to Mark Lloyd, Director of Sport explain how we teach sport at Great Walstead.

These combine to give a sporting experience that captures excellence, inclusivity, and enjoyment for all. Whether it’s competing in a national final, or playing a new sport for the first time, every sporting achievement is valued and recognised.

After-school clubs extend the fun even further, with opportunities to try sailing, karate, dance, horse riding and golf. With so much on offer, every child finds their place, their confidence and a lifelong love of sport.

pageCache.pageTitle: Wellbeing for years 7 & 8 | Great Walstead School
pageCache.text:
Wellbeing
Growing Independence, Strong Foundations
In Years 7 and 8, our focus is on helping pupils grow in independence while maintaining strong emotional foundations. We support both pupils and parents through open communication, pastoral care and practical guidance on navigating the pressures of adolescence and technology.
As children reach Years 7 and 8, life can become more complex. New friendships, growing independence and digital pressures all play a part in shaping these final years before senior school. At Great Walstead, wellbeing remains at the centre of everything we do.
Our tutor system continues to be a vital link between pupils, teachers and home; offering guidance, perspective and time to talk. Tutors know their pupils well and are there to listen, support and celebrate their progress, both in and out of the classroom.
We also work closely with parents, providing information sessions and practical support on the challenges that often emerge at this stage. Topics such as navigating technology, managing mobile phones and developing healthy online habits are explored together, helping families stay consistent and confident in their approach.
We believe in protecting childhood for as long as possible, encouraging pupils to enjoy real connections, outdoor play and face-to-face friendships. By nurturing these habits early, we help our pupils enter senior school as confident, balanced young people who are ready to face the next stage of life with strength and optimism.
Together, we create a community where children feel safe, confident and ready to face every new challenge with curiosity, kindness and courage.
ISI Report 2025 Highlights
“Pupils respect each other and are appropriately prepared to play a positive role in society.” Independent Schools Inspectorate, November 2025

Senior Success
Making us proud
Over the last five years an average of 35% of our Year 8 leavers have obtained a scholarship to their senior school. These include academic, sporting, music, drama and art as individual scholarships but also a number gaining ‘all-rounder’ awards where they have shown real talent in more than one area.
Our most recent leavers performed brilliantly and were offered 16 scholarships including four academic scholarships to top performing senior schools in Sussex. It’s a testament to the hard work of the pupils themselves as well as the teachers and parents who have supported them so strongly throughout.
All prospective scholars are supported in their studies. Talents are nurtured through additional after school clubs and activities, which adds strength to each pupil’s application. In addition, children showing potential in Year 6 to achieve a scholarship at 13+ are able to apply for an internal scholarship at 11+ in academic, drama, music, sport and art.
As well as internal Great Walstead scholarships, those of our Year 6 students who choose Ardingly College for their senior school are eligible to apply for the Ardingly Family of Schools Scholarships, which are held at Great Walstead in Years 7 and 8 and then at Ardingly College from Year 9.

pageCache.pageTitle: Opening Our Pre-Prep Library with Author Abie Longstaff | Great Walstead School
pageCache.text:
Starting a new chapter with Author Abie Longstaff
At Great Walstead School, we believe that a love of reading opens doors to imagination, confidence and lifelong learning. So there could hardly have been a better moment to celebrate the opening of our brand new Pre-Prep Library than during World Book Day week, with a visit from bestselling children’s author Abie Longstaff.
A Library Designed to Inspire
Our new Pre-Prep Library has been carefully created as a welcoming and inspiring space where children can discover books they love, enjoy storytelling together and begin to develop confidence as independent readers.
With colourful shelves, cosy corners and hundreds of stories waiting to be explored, the library is already becoming a place where imagination thrives. Opening it during World Book Day week felt especially meaningful, reinforcing the role that reading plays at the heart of our school.
A Space Where Stories Come Alive
As Alice Rees, Head of English, explains:
“Reading builds vocabulary, strengthens comprehension and gives children the confidence to explore more complex ideas across every subject. Just as importantly, stories nurture imagination, empathy and curiosity about the world around us.”
The new library has been designed to support exactly that: a space where children experience reading not simply as a skill to learn, but as something joyful to explore.
Inspiring Young Storytellers
Throughout the day, Abie Longstaff delivered four workshops, each tailored to the different age groups taking part.
For our Pre-School children, along with some parents who joined the session, Abie read her charming story Little Fairy Godmother. She then led an interactive mini-workshop exploring where story ideas come from, encouraging the children to see that inspiration can be found everywhere.
Later in the day, Reception to Year 2 pupils and parents, enjoyed another reading of Little Fairy Godmother. Abie then invited the children to imagine their own story ideas inspired by the familiar nursery rhyme Jack and Jill. The room quickly filled with ideas as pupils began thinking about the characters and their own adventures.
Unlocking the Magic of Ideas
For pupils in Years 3 to 5, the focus turned to the writing process itself. Abie spoke about how she has always been fascinated by secret doors and hidden spaces, which eventually inspired her book series The Trapdoor Mysteries.
Working in pairs, pupils were challenged to design their own magical doors or trapdoors. They thought about where the door might be hidden, what lay behind it and who might be trying to access it. The exercise quickly captured imaginations, showing just how easily creativity can take hold when children are given the freedom to explore.
A Behind-the-Scenes Look at Publishing
For our Years 6 to 8 pupils, the session offered a different perspective. Abie spoke about the publishing world behind the books they read, sharing insight into cover design, illustration, marketing and the journey a story takes from an idea to a finished book.
It was a fascinating look at the creative industry behind storytelling and gave pupils a deeper appreciation of how the books they love are brought to life.
A Celebration of Reading
One of the most memorable parts of the day was simply seeing how engaged the pupils were. Across every workshop, children eagerly contributed ideas, asked thoughtful questions and shared their creativity with confidence.
The celebrations concluded with the official ribbon-cutting ceremony, led by Abie herself, before parents and pupils were invited to explore the new Pre-Prep Library together for the first time.
Seeing families browsing the shelves, discovering favourite authors and sharing stories together was the perfect way to begin this new chapter for Great Walstead’s youngest readers.
A Lifelong Love of Reading
At Great Walstead, reading is woven into everyday school life through our libraries, classroom learning and shared storytelling. But the strongest reading habits are built when school and families work together.
Whether it is sharing a bedtime story, listening to an audiobook in the car or discovering a new favourite series, these small moments help children build confidence, curiosity and a lifelong connection with books.
With our new Pre-Prep Library now open, we cannot wait to see the many adventures our pupils discover within its shelves.
And if the creativity sparked during Abie Longstaff’s visit is anything to go by, the next generation of storytellers may already be sitting among them.
See Great Walstead in Action
If you would like to discover more about Great Walstead’s learning culture and how we nurture curiosity, creativity and a love of reading from the very earliest years, we would love to welcome you to the school.
Book a personalised tour and see our children learning, exploring and discovering their passions every day.

pageCache.pageTitle: Nurturing Potential: A Message from Headteacher | Great Walstead School
pageCache.text:
How Great Walstead’s Scholarship Programme celebrates talent, curiosity and ambition.
At Great Walstead School, we believe every child has a spark - a talent, passion or skill that deserves to be acknowledged and nurtured. Whether it’s a love of academia, music, art, drama or sport, our role is to help each pupil find what makes them tick and to support them in developing it to the highest level.
“At Great Walstead, we want children to be brave enough to discover their strengths, and confident enough to pursue them.” - Chris Calvey, Headteacher
Celebrating Talent and Opportunity
From Year 6 onwards, pupils who demonstrate exceptional ability and enthusiasm can apply for one of our 11+ Scholarships. These awards celebrate excellence across key areas - academic, art, drama, music, and sport - and provide opportunities for enrichment, leadership and growth.
Scholars receive an academic award (which may open a bursary route where needed), alongside bespoke opportunities to refine their skills through specialist enrichment programmes.
“As a Scholar, I’m being pushed to think deeply, make links and work hard.” - Heidi, Year 8
These enrichment experiences are designed to extend learning beyond the classroom -through workshops, competitions, performances and creative collaborations. Whether it’s joining our Performing Arts programme, training with our specialist sports coaches, or exploring new techniques with visiting artists, every opportunity helps scholars grow in confidence and character.
Part of a Family of Schools
Running alongside our internal scholarships is the Ardingly Family of Schools Award, which mirrors the Great Walstead approach and continues through to senior education at Ardingly College. This ensures long-term support and continuity for children who wish to follow that pathway.
Our aim is simple: to nurture and develop each pupil’s individual strengths so that, when the time comes, they are fully prepared to apply for scholarships to the senior school of their choice.
We’re proud of our track record of success across disciplines, with pupils earning awards to respected independent schools including Brighton College, Hurstpierpoint College, Bede’s, Worth, and further afield to Wellington College and Millfield School.
“I love being on the stage performing with our band. Being a music scholar is amazing and I love being part of chamber choir, orchestra, wood wind ensemble, tea-time concerts, and Christmas concerts to name just a few.” - Max, Year 8
More Than an Award
Scholarship life at Great Walstead is about more than recognition, it’s about growth, challenge and character. Each scholar is encouraged to demonstrate the school’s core values and the 7Cs - Curiosity, Courage, Creativity, Collaboration, Compassion, Commitment and Confidence which run through everything we do.
“Our scholarship programme is as much about nurturing the person as it is about developing the talent. We want children to leave us not only skilled, but grounded, kind and ready for whatever comes next.” - Chris Calvey, Headteacher

Performing Arts
The buzz of performing arts is a huge part of Great Walstead. Art, music and drama are integrated as part of the curriculum for all ages with plentiful performance opportunities. Plus our on-site working art studio means children have access and insight into a range of artistic media.
Drama
From Year 3 onward, drama is taught as part of the weekly timetable and children study a wide variety of topics ranging from Greek theatre to silent movies or improvisation.
All children are encouraged to develop their confidence and collaborative skills by taking part and sharing work with fellow classmates. Support and kindness are used to promote an environment where children are comfortable to perform either individually or as part of a group.
There are numerous opportunities throughout the year to be part of year-group productions, short plays and presentations as well as the highly anticipated school musical.
We organise regular trips to the theatre, both in the surrounding areas and to the West End. This offers each year group a chance to see some fantastic shows such as Wicked, Matilda and The Lion King as well as a selection of less conventional performances.
Music
Music is everywhere at Great Walstead. From visiting musicians giving concerts to the many rehearsals and performances by our own budding talent.
All children have music lessons as part of the curriculum. These involve a varied syllabus of academic study, encompassing elements of performance, composition and music appreciation.
Outside of the classroom every year group up to and including Year 6 has a weekly choir session and one-to-one lessons are offered for piano, singing and all orchestral instruments.
We also have an auditioned chamber choir and an orchestra, plus a host of other smaller instrumental ensembles such as brass ensemble and wind. All these groups rehearse before or after school and perform at a year-round series of concerts and services.
Music and drama are closely linked at Great Walstead, and each term our Performing Arts Thursday is staged to showcase a selection of works performed by various year groups. There is a full school production in the Spring term, involving Years 6 to 8 coming together for a much-anticipated music and drama extravaganza.
Art
Our children benefit from the positive values of art education, where creativity inspires both personal and cognitive development, alongside an invaluable means of expression and awareness of visual culture and the wider world.
There are no boundaries to creativity. From our very youngest pupils to those aiming for art scholarships at senior level, everyone is encouraged to create, reach their goals and enjoy the act of making.
We provide the opportunity for children to experiment with an extensive range of materials including painting and drawing, mixed media, printing, sculpture and ceramics, as well as engaging in collaborative projects within the school and local community.
Finally, there’s valuable real-world input from our artists in residence: a group of professional artists who are based at school and offer additional clubs and the possibility to work alongside them in a professional art studio.

SEN (Supported learning)
Meeting Individual Needs
Every child learns differently, and at Great Walstead we celebrate those differences. Our Learning Enhancement Department provides thoughtful, personalised support that helps each pupil build confidence, develop skills and thrive within the classroom and beyond.
Right in the centre of the school, overlooking the Atrium and beautiful grounds, you will find our kind, purposeful and nurturing Learning Enhancement Department. It is a welcoming space where support, encouragement and progress go hand in hand.
Our team of five qualified specialists work closely with teachers across the School to identify and support individual learning needs. The focus is on strengthening literacy and numeracy skills, boosting confidence and developing strategies for independent learning.
Most children receive support within their regular classroom setting from teachers who understand their individual learning styles. Where helpful, additional small group or one-to-one sessions are offered to reinforce key skills and address specific challenges. Some of these interventions are available as an enhancement at an additional cost.
The department also provides assessments, guidance and referrals to external specialists where needed, such as educational psychologists, occupational therapists or speech and language therapists. Parents are supported throughout the process, ensuring communication and understanding remain strong.
At Great Walstead, our approach is collaborative. Teachers, parents and pupils work together to build on strengths, overcome challenges and celebrate every success. The result is confident learners who feel supported, capable and proud of their progress.
ISI Report 2025 Highlights
"Pupils who have special educational needs and/or disabilities receive individual support in lessons and make consistently good progress." Independent Schools Inspectorate, November 2025

ISI Inspection Report Highlights 2025
November 2025
The Independent Schools Inspectorate (ISI) inspects independent schools for the Department for Education, offering an objective view of school life.
This page shares a short, parent-friendly summary of what inspectors observed during their recent visit to Great Walstead School.
Hear from the Headmaster
It was very special to see that, in their short time with us, the ISI inspectors were able to capture the essence of Great Walstead School.
They recognised that our pupils enjoy their lessons, apply themselves diligently and are supported by teachers who hold ambitious expectations for their learning. I was also delighted to see the inspectors note how learning takes place both inside and outside the classroom - something we see as central to developing a genuine love of learning, particularly in the younger years.
The inspection looks far beyond classroom activity alone, and it was lovely to see the inspectors recognise the support and care pupils show towards one another across the school. Overall, the report reflects the academic ambition we hold for our children, achieved within a community where kindness and respect are lived every day.Chris Calvey,Headmaster
What stands out
The ISI report highlights a school where pupils are encouraged to work hard, think deeply and enjoy learning. Teaching is ambitious and well planned, while lessons remain engaging, dynamic and responsive to pupils’ needs.
Learning at Great Walstead extends well beyond the classroom. Inspectors recognised the value of learning both indoors and outdoors, with the school’s woodland environment playing an important role in fostering curiosity, exploration and respect for the natural world - particularly in the Early Years.
Just as importantly, inspectors saw a community built on strong values. Pupils treat one another with respect, care and kindness, and are supported to grow not only academically, but socially, emotionally and morally. Opportunities to build confidence, character and leadership are woven throughout school life, helping pupils develop into thoughtful, resilient and self-assured young people.
Report themes at a glance
What the inspectors noticed about learning, care and character.
Academic Ambition & Teaching Excellence
Teaching is expert, well-paced and ambitious, helping pupils enjoy learning while making strong progress.
Learning Indoors and Outdoors
The curriculum extends beyond the classroom, with outdoor learning enriching understanding and engagement.
Personalised Progress
Assessment informs tailored support and challenge, ensuring every pupil, including those with SEND or EAL, can thrive.
Character, Confidence & Values
Respect, kindness and care underpin school life, alongside opportunities to build confidence and self-belief.
Early Years Foundations
Children develop independence, language and physical confidence through purposeful play and exploration.
ISI Report Highlights
A summary of independent findings from our November 2025 inspection.
Teaching that is ambitious and enjoyable
Pupils enjoy their lessons, apply themselves diligently and are supported by teachers who hold high expectations for their learning, helping them make strong progress.
“Pupils thrive in their learning and make good progress.” – Independent Schools Inspectorate
A Curriculum that inspires curiosity
The curriculum is broad, balanced and designed to prepare pupils well for future success, with specialist teaching supporting older pupils as they prepare for senior school.
“The curriculum extends learning both indoors and outside the classroom.” – Independent Schools Inspectorate
Learning beyond the classroom
Outdoor learning plays an important role in pupils’ development, encouraging exploration, creativity and a genuine love of learning, particularly in the younger years.
“Teachers place emphasis on learning both indoors and outside the classroom.” – Independent Schools Inspectorate
A caring, values-led community
Inspectors recognised the respect, support and care pupils show towards one another, reflecting the school’s strong moral values and positive culture.
“Pupils respect each other and are appropriately prepared to play a positive role in society.” – Independent Schools Inspectorate
Strong foundations in Early Years
Children in the Early Years develop confidence, independence and strong language skills through carefully planned play, outdoor activity and supportive relationships.
“Children learn and develop confidently and effectively.” – Independent Schools Inspectorate
What this means for your child
An ISI report provides independent reassurance that a school meets nationally set standards and delivers on its educational promises. For families considering Great Walstead, the report confirms that Great Walstead offers:
Together, these elements can create an environment where children feel happy, supported and inspired to do their best.

Walstead Unwrapped
Igniting curiosity one episode at a time.
Walstead Unwrapped is a pupil-led podcast that sparks curiosity, celebrates young voices and explores the ideas, stories and questions that matter most to our school community.
A Message from Chris
Working alongside our Year 8 prefects on Walstead Unwrapped has been a genuine privilege. I have watched them grow as leaders and collaborators, gaining confidence while planning, producing and sharing a podcast that truly reflects their curiosity and spirit.
The making of Walstead Unwrapped
Creating the Podcast
Enthusiasm for the podcast was high from the get-go, with staff, pupils and parents alike instantly voicing their support! The idea was to provide an opportunity for pupils to share their perspectives, explore big questions and create something meaningful the whole community could engage with.
Recruiting the Podcasters
The decision was made to begin the podcast with the Year 8 Prefects as we developed the podcast’s identity and focus. The team have thrown themselves into the opportunity, bringing their enthusiasm and unique perspectives to Walstead Unwrapped.
Name, Logo & Jingle
Prefects formed a clear vision for the podcast’s identity. After briefing the marketing team, they saw their ideas realised in a distinctive logo, with a jingle following shortly after.
Episode Ideas
Topics are chosen based on the topics that are hot in school at the time. From big questions like what makes a good teacher to why sport and the arts are important, each topic unleashes their enthusiasm and curiosity and provides a wonderful opportunity for thoughtful and constructive discussion.
Recording
Now the fun really begins. With everyone contributing, the Prefects support one another to communicate confidently, listen carefully and keep conversations engaging.
Editing
Episodes are then reviewed and edited by the marketing team, improving clarity and flow while ensuring the final programme represents the original idea behind the topic. The podcast team reviews the final output before it goes live.
Going Live
The release of every episode is a proud milestone, marking the journey from initial idea to a finished production shared with listeners.
In the Future
We hope to expand the podcast to invite more voices to participate, making for an even more vibrant, inclusive representation of life here at Great Walstead.
Listen to Walstead Unwrapped

Scholarships
Everything you need to know about the scholarships we offer and how to apply
We offer a limited number of 11+ scholarships in Year 6 across the different disciplines of school life to those pupils who show both high levels of interest and potential. Awards are offered to pupils who, in our view, are likely candidates for a similar award as they move into their senior school at 13+. Our 11+ scholarships are offered for academic, sport, drama, music and art.Children applying for these scholarships are expected to be working at a high level in their field. The benchmark for awarding scholarships will be senior schools’ expectations of potential scholars at 13+. Pupils’ general conduct and approach to school life will also be an important factor in the decision-making process.Dates for Year 6 scholarships will be announced at the end of the Spring Term.Pupils may apply for a maximum of two scholarships. If a pupil were to win two awards, one would be honorary.Scholarships will carry a value of between £300 and £1000 per year off fees.
SCHOLARSHIPS: 11+ (NEW CRITERIA)
Please note internal candidates will not need to submit an application form as pupils will now be nominated by the relevant Heads of Departments. External candidates should complete a form as part of the application process.
As well as these internal Great Walstead scholarships, those of our Year 6 students who choose Ardingly College for their senior school are eligible to apply for the Ardingly Family of Schools Scholarships, which are held at Great Walstead in Years 7 and 8 and then at Ardingly College from Year 9.
Our scholarships
Any questions should be directed to Emma Scotland (Deputy Head Academic) emma.scotland@greatwalstead.co.uk
Academic Scholarships
Internal candidates: there will be no formal examinations for internal candidates. All children will be assessed in English, maths, science through regular in-class assessments alongside non-verbal and verbal tests taken in Autumn 2025. Those pupils performing at the very top end of their year group academically and demonstrating strengths across a range of subject areas will be awarded scholarships. Should they win an award, they will be expected to display a high level of maturity, diligence, initiative and independence in their approach towards their studies in the Seniors. There would be an expectation to be involved in some extracurricular activities and possibly external competitions, as well as take on certain responsibilities which relate to their role.
External candidates: will sit papers in English, maths and science. Non-verbal and verbal tests will also be set for external candidates. Pupils who apply for this scholarship should be performing at the very top end of their year group academically and demonstrate strengths across a range of subject areas. Should they win an award, they will be expected to display a high level of maturity, diligence, initiative and independence in their approach towards their studies in the seniors. There would be an expectation to be involved in some extracurricular activities and possibly external competitions, as well as take on certain responsibilities which relate to their role. These assessments will take place during a taster day as part of the application process.
Art Scholarships
Children applying for an Art Scholarship should be able to demonstrate and express their exceptional talent, commitment and ability for the subject. They will be required to verbalise their passion for Art discussing recent exhibitions and workshops attended and present a body of work created beyond school. Successful Art Scholars will be expected to: attend an Art Scholars’ session every week (after school), alongside a session with our ‘Artists in residence’ session during a school day rest period, complete a minimum of two hours of artwork at home each week, complete holiday tasks, submit work for school competitions or art events, and visit a minimum of three galleries or exhibitions during the year.
Internal candidates: Pupils will be assessed through in class observations and assessments.
External candidates: will be invited to take part in an art class and should present a portfolio that clearly demonstrates their fluent skills across the following disciplines: observational drawing, painting, sculpture, textiles, printing, mixed media and photography. This assessment will take place during a taster day as part of the application process.
Drama Scholarships
Drama Scholarships will be given to candidates who can confidently express their distinct talents, and have clear enthusiasm and commitment for Drama and Theatre. They must also have a desire to be regularly and actively involved in supporting the Drama Department at Great Walstead. Participating in performances and plays at Great Walstead, or in extra-curricular drama activities, will be viewed as scholarly attributes. Any participation in examination programmes, such as Trinity College London, LAMDA, or Trinity Guildhall, would be regarded as positive evidence of a candidate's experience, but most certainly not essential for applying. Drama Scholars will be expected to be involved in all performing arts events. Scholars will regularly watch productions, read plays and actively seek to further their knowledge and experience in Drama and Theatre. In Year 8, Drama Scholars will be prepared for scholarships to their senior school.
Internal candidates: Will be assessed through their work in lessons and in their commitment to drama.
External candidates: will be invited to take part in a drama class. Candidates will also be asked to sight-read a piece of unseen text/section of a play. They will be expected to discuss their interest in drama and why they have applied for the Drama Scholarship in an interview with the Head of Drama. They should bring with them a portfolio to further enhance their audience, showing any evidence of their experience to date (shows they have seen/been involved in, theatre/play reviews, photographs and certificates) which will be discussed and referred to in the interview. This assessment will take place during a taster day as part of the application process.
Music Scholarships
Children applying for a Music Scholarship should be performing pieces of at least Grade 4 standard (on their first-choice study instrument (which can be voice), plus a second instrument (at about Grade 2 level). Candidates will be expected to display an outstanding commitment to ensemble music making and become a high-profile musician within the school community. In Year 8, scholars must actively seek to broaden their knowledge of different musical genres, attend concerts of varying repertoire and be able to engage passionately in discussion. Additional experience in external training orchestras and groups is desirable though not compulsory. Pupils will demonstrate maturity, determination and take pride in their music making both inside and outside of the classroom.
Internal candidates: will be recommended by the Head of Music in consultation with visiting music teachers.
External candidates: will be required to play one piece on their main instrument (which can be voice), plus one on their second instrument (at about Grade 2 level). The singing of a popular melody will also be expected. In addition, there will be some aural and sight-reading tests appropriate to the recommended grades. This assessment will take place during a taster day as part of the application process.
Sport Scholarships
Children applying for a Sport Scholarship should be able to demonstrate exceptional ability and potential in two of the major sports on offer here at Great Walstead. These pupils will be working well beyond the expected level of their year group with a strong understanding of the key principles and tactical ideas of the major sports at school. They will have strong game sense and awareness in team related sports and will shine in 'A team' situations. They will be able to perform well under pressure, lifting their performance when challenged. These pupils will have appropriate fitness and athletic levels required to perform at a high level. Conduct, attitude and effort in both training and matches will be taken into account.
This award is an all-round sport award. Pupils who excel in one sport may still be considered for a sport specific scholarship to their chosen senior school (supported by the Director of Sport), even if they do not gain an all-round sport scholarship whilst at Great Walstead.
Pupils who receive this award will be expected to uphold the highest standards of attitude and sportsmanship, acting as a role model for their peers and sport as a whole at Great Walstead. They will be expected to represent the school in any fixtures/events for which they are selected during the week and, occasionally, at the weekend.
Internal candidates: will be nominated by the Head of Sport in consultation with the whole games department.
External candidates: will be invited to take part in a games lesson and asked to demonstrate their core skills across 2 chosen sports. They will be expected to talk about their passion for sport and be playing at the appropriate level in teams in or outside of school. This assessment will take place during a taster day as part of the application process.

Artists in Residence
A collaboration with Brighton University School of Art.
We are a collective of Brighton Alumni who have recently renovated the art studio courtyard and begun practicing and creating in this space. Our work ranges from ceramic work, both functional ware and sculptural pieces to objects in wood and metal.
We have begun teaching after school clubs to the children and are offering a range of parent workshops during the school day.
Isobel Roope
BA (Hons) 3D Design and Craft
I am a ceramic artist living and working in Sussex and a recent graduate from the University of Brighton. I create sculptural forms – some closed, some open. The surface is finished in either a smoke or saggar firing technique or with oxides, the smoke firing is done in the walled garden. I have some work available for sale and I take commissions too. A selection of my work can be seen via my Instagram page.
Alma Boyes
With an established background in ceramic practice spanning over 40 years, my current work explores the historic technique of agateware which was prominent in the UK in 17th & 18th century industrial ceramics, notably Josiah Wedgewood. The term ‘Agateware’ refers to ceramic pieces made from coloured or mixed clays and mimics the multicoloured appearance of agate stone. I am drawn to this technique because of the unique combinations of colour and pattern which are created using the throwing process on the pottery wheel. My collection of works include large lidded vessels, some of which I adorn with hand-modelled birds – predominately British species including blackbirds, crows and sparrows. This new work brings together my experiences of designing and producing industrial ceramics, with many years specialising in portraits and sculptures of endangered species for bronze casting.
Rosie Tweedale
I am a designer maker working with natural materials, clay and wood. My projects have involved collaborating closely with local community organisations to create socially engaged craft objects which tell each of their stories.
I recently completed a ceramics residency in Denmark where I explored the material dualism between clay and wood. I used wood-firing techniques and ash glazes to create ceramic woodgrain vessels that embody aspects of the forest. I am driven by the importance of connecting to our natural environments using local materials, which I will be integrating into my workshops this year.
Zahra Priddle
Zahra Priddle is an accomplished jewellery designer turned sculptor whose fascination since childhood for architectural forms and monumental structures led her to consider scaling her work. It was while studying for her Masters, that she began to experiment with new materials, techniques and processes. The nature of her investigation was to map a process of scaling her hand manipulated paper forms to create medium and large scale sculptural pieces for interior spaces, incorporating both digital and analogue methods.
A graduate of Central Saint Martins, Zahra achieved a First Class Honours Degree in Jewellery Design in 1994. After success with her degree show, she caught the attention of Donna Karan who invited her to design accessories in New York. She subsequently returned to London and alongside establishing her own label, took a position with Japanese fine jewellers, Mikimoto Pearls. From 2006 to 2014, Zahra relocated with her family abroad where she continued to develop her artistic practice. She returned to study a Masters in Craft at the University of Brighton, graduating with Distinction in 2019.

Celebrating 100 years
We are delighted to have celebrated our centenary in 2025: 1925-2025. Over the last 100 years Great Walstead School has seen a great deal of change as the site itself has been developed and the school has grown and evolved into one of the leading co-educational day schools. At the same time it has kept its very special feel promoting and developing pupils' determination, adventurous spirit and love of life, and genuine empathy for those people around them.
1925-2025 A hundred years of education & adventure
One of the things that makes Great Walstead so special is the way the teachers throughout its hundred-year history have made the children's learning experience so exciting and adventurous. Outdoor learning is an integral part of school life which has enabled our pupils to be ambitious and excited about their learning. Our youngest pupils have followed the tracks of dinosaurs through our words as they embark on new learning experiences while the older pupils rally their teams as they prepare for Q-Day. All this is accomplished while at the same time securing academic, sporting, musical, art and drama success at a range of prestigious senior schools. We are certainly a school of lots of mud and lots of love!
OUR History
Founded in 1925 by RJ Mowll as a boys’ boarding school, Great Walstead School has developed into a thriving co-educational day school for children from 2½ to 13 years.
From September 2024, we will be running a programme of events to mark this milestone with opportunities to remember how the Victorian house at its heart became the modern educational establishment we see today.
Moreover, the wonderful woods remain a key part of the school and OGWs will be pleased to know that the tradition of Q-Day lives on.
A word from our headmaster
It is such a pleasure to be Headmaster at Great Walstead School and I feel a bit of a fraud calling it work. I am surrounded by kind and caring pupils and staff who throw themselves into every part of Walstead life with such commitment. Pupils at Great Walstead have a genuine love of learning where they are always up for taking on a challenge and will always learn from things that don't work as planned. Because of this attitude I believe they are well-rounded, resilient and happy children. Please do keep in touch, we would love to hear from you.
Chris Calvey, Headmaster
Join the Old Great Walsteadians
We would love to keep you up to date with everything that is happening at Great Walstead for our centenary year and beyond.
